outcome.answer: The closest study finds that emotion recognition benefits most from recent conversational context, with roughly 90% of the gain captured by the latest 10–30 preceding turns, depending on the emotion-label set. Sadness benefits especially from context, while discourse-marker position—including markers at sentence beginnings—is associated with emotion; sad utterances have fewer left-periphery markers than other emotions. The paper does not establish that sentence starters themselves identify mood or specify a minimum number of turns needed for reliable identification. [1]
